text.p: Universal International Inc said on Wednesday that it expects to post a profit in the fourth quarter, but a loss for the full year 1996.
The company reported a third quarter loss of $0.20 a share versus a profit of $0.05 last year.
"Based upon the continued losses realized during the third quarter, we are now projecting that we will incur a loss for all of 1996," chief executive Mark Ravich said in a statement.
Ravich said the company plans to stabilize retail operations at the current level to "to pause and recover from the stress of expanding from 22 to 72 stores over the past 21 months".
Universal now operates a total of 72 stores, 50 under the Only Deals name and 22 under the Odd's-N-End's name.
It said Richard Ennen accepted the position of President of its Only Deals Inc unit.

"Although we are disappointed with the results for the first nine months of 1996, we believe that the investment in new stores, coupled with the new leadership under Mr. Ennen has positioned the company for a profitable fourth quarter and a return to profitability in 1997 even if no new retail stores are opened next year," Ravich said.
